claim: Sparse training signal (not model architecture or compute) is the binding constraint on Quality Model X's accuracy ceiling

angles.name: industry_competitive
angles.instruction: Survey peer ML model teams (internal and external). Who has hit similar accuracy plateaus? What was the binding constraint they identified?

angles.name: internal_owners
angles.instruction: Pull all Quality Model X experiment results from the past 4 quarters. Categorize by intervention type (architecture, compute, signal). What's the lift distribution per category?

angles.name: problem_framing
angles.instruction: Decompose 'binding constraint' — could be data, architecture, compute, eval, or labeling. Map each to evidence pro/con.

angles.name: measurement
angles.instruction: What's the eval methodology for Quality Model X? Are we measuring the right thing? Could the plateau be a metric ceiling, not a model ceiling?

angles.name: adjacent_tech
angles.instruction: What new signal sources or augmentation techniques (LLM-judged labels, weak supervision, distillation) is the team not yet using?

angles.name: user_research
angles.instruction: What does UXR / qualitative interview data say about how end-users experience low-quality model outputs? Does any of it hint at the constraint type the model agents miss?
